title: The Wrong Visitor
premise: Isandro Quintana takes a teaching post in a remote mountain town where students have been vanishing for generations, always 'moved away,' never heard from again. When Isandro's sleep-recording app captures a second voice answering questions Isandro never asked aloud, they discover the town's founding families have been feeding children to something beneath the old well to keep it asleep. The voice belongs to Marisol, the first missing child, who has waited decades for an outsider with no family debt to the town. Isandro must choose between the quiet safety of complicity and helping the remaining at-risk children escape before the autumn equinox, when the well 'refills' and demands its count — even if that means burning the town's covenant and their own career, reputation, and possibly life.
about_author: Emrys Whitlock is the pen name of a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in isolated mountain communities before turning to horror full-time. They write about institutions that protect themselves instead of children, drawing on folklore collected from former colleagues across three countries.

chapters.title: The Position Nobody Wanted
chapters.summary: Third-person limited, Isandro. Arriving in Hoya del Cielo after a scandal at their last school, Isandro notices the town's too-perfect welcome and the classroom roster with suspicious gaps. Emotional beat: cautious hope shadowed by unease.

chapters.title: Twenty-Six Desks
chapters.summary: Isandro counts desks against enrollment records and finds seven extra chairs, worn smooth by use. The principal, Doña Reyes, deflects smoothly. Beat: first crack in the town's facade; Isandro's instinct for patterns awakens.

chapters.title: Moved Away
chapters.summary: A student, Tomás, mentions his cousin 'went to live with the well' then goes pale and silent. Isandro files it as childish idiom. Beat: dread planted, dismissed — the reader sees what Isandro won't yet admit.

chapters.title: The Recording Habit
chapters.summary: Establishing chapter: insomniac Isandro plays sleep recordings to check for night terrors, a habit from therapy. The recordings are mundane — until one ends with breathing that isn't theirs. Beat: isolation established as vulnerability.

chapters.title: Parent Night
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to Doña Reyes. She watches Isandro charm the parents and notes which families flinch when certain names are mentioned. Beat: antagonist introduced through her weary devotion to duty.

chapters.title: The Second Voice
chapters.summary: Isandro, third-person limited. A recording captures a girl's voice answering questions Isandro never asked: 'No. Not yet. He still sleeps.' Isandro tells themselves it's radio interference. Beat: denial cracking into obsession.

chapters.title: Marisol Vidal, 1974
chapters.summary: In the school archive, Isandro finds a class photo from 1974 with one face scratched out. The librarian, old Señor Anselmo, says the name Marisol Vidal like a warning. Beat: the past has teeth.

chapters.title: Questions in the Dark
chapters.summary: Isandro begins asking the recording questions deliberately, leaving the recorder running overnight. The voice answers: she is cold, she is many, she is waiting for someone unafraid. Beat: forbidden intimacy — love beginning where fear should be.

chapters.title: Tomás Stops Coming
chapters.summary: Tomás is absent. His mother says the family 'got an opportunity downriver.' His desk sits empty among the extras. Beat: grief and guilt; the pattern is real and Isandro arrived mid-count.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: Anselmo, drunk, tells Isandro the covenant: every generation, the town gives the well its count or the thing below wakes hungry. He begs Isandro to stop asking questions. Beat: exposition delivered as confession; moral stakes named.

chapters.title: Doña Reyes Offers Tea
chapters.summary: Reyes gently warns Isandro off, revealing she lost her own sister to the count and chose duty over truth. Beat: antagonist humanized; the theme of loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: What the Voice Wants
chapters.summary: Marisol's voice grows clearer: she doesn't want revenge, she wants the remaining children out before equinox, when the well refills and the count must be met. Beat: the mission crystallizes; hope entangled with horror.

chapters.title: Family Debt
chapters.summary: Isandro researches land deeds and learns every founding family holds a 'well share' — including, shockingly, the deed signed by Isandro's landlord, meaning Isandro now lives inside the covenant. Beat: personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: The First Child on the List
chapters.summary: Marisol names the next child owed: little Inés Barrios. Isandro watches Inés at recess, laughing, and cannot eat that night. Beat: love against duty begins — Isandro loves these children already.

chapters.title: A Plan Made of Paper
chapters.summary: Isandro drafts escape plans: bus schedules, forged transfer letters, safe houses downriver. Marisol corrects them through the recorder — she knows which roads the town watches. Beat: alliance deepens into tenderness.

chapters.title: Caught Listening
chapters.summary: Reyes discovers Isandro's recorder during a classroom inspection but returns it, saying only, 'Some voices are better unheard.' Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; ambiguous mercy.

chapters.title: Inés Disappears Early
chapters.summary: The town moves the schedule up — Inés is taken days ahead of the count, panic in the covenant. Isandro finds her ribbon at the wellhead. Beat: despair; the machinery accelerates beyond control.

chapters.title: Down the Old Stair
chapters.summary: Compelled by Marisol's voice, Isandro descends the sealed stair behind the wellhouse and glimpses the vast dark below — and dozens of small lights, like held breaths. Beat: awe and terror fused; the horror given scale.

chapters.title: The Lights Have Names
chapters.summary: Below, Isandro learns the missing aren't consumed but kept, suspended, part of the thing's dream. Marisol chose to stay so others could leave someday. Beat: tragic nobility; the cost of loyalty revealed.

chapters.title: Reyes Finds Them
chapters.summary: Reyes catches Isandro at the stair, gun drawn, but cannot shoot — Isandro speaks her sister's name, learned from Marisol. Beat: climax of the loyalty-vs-truth duel; Reyes wavers.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: The town elders offer Isandro a place in the covenant — safety, belonging, a family — if they forget the children. Isandro refuses. Beat: the theme stated outright; point of no return.

chapters.title: Burning the Ledger
chapters.summary: Isandro steals the covenant ledger naming every debt and burns it on the schoolhouse steps, declaring the count void. The town erupts. Beat: justice outside the law, defiant and reckless.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: The town seals the school; families split between covenant loyalists and the terrified few who side with Isandro. Beat: siege atmosphere; allies gathered at terrible cost.

chapters.title: What Wakes Hungry
chapters.summary: With the ledger burned, the well stirs early. The ground hums; wells run backward; dogs go silent. Marisol warns there is no more time. Beat: ticking clock made physical.

chapters.title: Nine Children, One Truck
chapters.summary: Isandro smuggles nine marked children out in a water truck through the orchard road while Reyes 'inspects' the checkpoint and looks away. Beat: hard-won hope; Reyes's defection completed.

chapters.title: The Count Comes Up Short
chapters.summary: At equinox midnight, the town gathers at the well and the count fails. The thing below begins to wake, and the kept lights begin to gutter. Beat: consequence arrives; victory curdles.

chapters.title: Marisol's Choice
chapters.summary: Marisol reveals the final truth: the well can be lulled back to sleep only if the kept ones are released willingly — and someone must carry the dream out in their place. Beat: sacrifice framed; emotional nadir.

chapters.title: Every Family Its Answer
chapters.summary: Isandro confronts each founding family, forcing them to choose: release their ancestors' victims or be named in what comes. Some kneel; some flee; some pick up tools. Beat: communal judgment; justice distributed.

chapters.title: The Well Opens
chapters.summary: The wellhouse splits open. What rises is less a creature than a hunger wearing the town's oldest memories. Isandro stands at the rim with the recorder playing Marisol's voice. Beat: full horror climax begins.

chapters.title: The Voice That Answers
chapters.summary: Isandro offers themselves as the new keeper — not as sacrifice to the hunger, but as the one voice it must answer, turning the covenant's logic against itself. Beat: courage as strategy; love weaponized.

chapters.title: Lights Rising
chapters.summary: One by one, the kept lights rise from the dark — Marisol last, pressing sixty years of names into Isandro's hands before dissolving toward dawn. Beat: catharsis; grief and gratitude braided.

chapters.title: What the Town Buried Instead
chapters.summary: The hunger, denied its count and given truth instead, collapses back into the deep, sated by acknowledgment rather than children. The town fills the well with the ledger's ashes. Beat: resolution of the supernatural contract.

chapters.title: Aftermath: Empty Chairs
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the seven extra desks are carried out and burned. Families of the long-missing receive letters written in Isandro's hand, each name restored. Beat: mourning made practical; closure without comfort.

chapters.title: Reyes Resigns
chapters.summary: Reyes turns herself and the town's history over to outside authorities, choosing truth at last, knowing it will destroy Hoya del Cielo's standing. Beat: her arc completes; justice enters lawful channels too late but fully.

chapters.title: The Children Downriver
chapters.summary: Isandro visits the nine escaped children in their new school, ordinary and loud and alive. Inés's ribbon is pinned inside Isandro's jacket. Beat: tenderness earned; why it was all worth it.

chapters.title: The Last Recording
chapters.summary: Isandro plays the final tape one last time: silence, then faintly, a child's laughter that fades like weather. They delete nothing and keep everything. Beat: haunting grace note; memory as monument.

chapters.title: A New Post
chapters.summary: Isandro accepts a teaching position in another forgotten town, eyes open this time, carrying a list of questions to ask on day one. Beat: transformed purpose; the vigilante teacher reborn.

chapters.title: Epilogue: The Second Visitor
chapters.summary: Years later, a stranger arrives in Hoya del Cielo asking about the well, and an elderly Isandro — visiting the rebuilt school — recognizes the look. Beat: cyclical dread softened into stewardship.

chapters.title: The Wrong Visitor
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Isandro's reflection: the town always believed the wrong visitor would be the monster. It was a teacher with a recorder and no family debt — the one thing the covenant couldn't price. Beat: thematic seal; quiet, resolute ending.
